titulo_es: The verb to be (Spanish ser and estar)
descripcion_es: Present and past of the verb to be: affirmative, negative and questions.
resumen: To be is the equivalent of both Spanish “ser” and “estar”. We use it for identity, origin, job, age, state, place and the weather; in the present it has three forms (am, is, are) and in the past two (was, were).

explicacion.texto: English has no difference between ser and estar: I am a teacher (es: soy profesor) and I am tired (es: estoy cansado) use the same verb. Also, age, hunger, cold and being right are expressed with to be, not with Spanish “tener”: I am 30, I am hungry.

filas: I'm not / she isn't / they aren't
Are you ready? Is it cold?
Was she at home? Were they late?
Yes, I am. / No, it isn't.
Yes, she was. / No, they weren't.

items: In questions the order changes: verb before subject (Is he Spanish?). Do is not used.
To make the negative, add not after the verb: She is not here.
With I the negative contraction is I'm not (“I amn't” does not exist).
In affirmative short answers there is no contraction: Yes, I am (not “Yes, I'm”).

ejemplos.frase: My name is Laura and I'm from Seville.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me llamo Laura y soy de Sevilla.

ejemplos.frase: Is the museum open on Mondays?
They weren't at the party last night.
ejemplos.traduccion: No estuvieron en la fiesta anoche.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Age is expressed with to be, not with have.
In English the subject is necessary; for the weather we use it.
To be does not use do in questions or negatives.
Hungry, thirsty, cold, hot and afraid go with to be.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with am, is or are.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the table of forms: with you, we and they the present of to be is are. The clue is the subject my parents, a plural that is the same as they. So the verb is are. In Spanish we would say “son”; English has no difference between ser and estar.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: My parents = they, which takes are.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Is is for he, she or it; my parents is plural (they) and takes are.
Be is the infinitive; you need the conjugated form: are.
Am is only used with I.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with am, is or are.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the table of forms: with I the present of to be is am. The clue is the subject I. Origin is expressed with be from: I am from Valencia (es: “soy de Valencia”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With I the present of to be is am.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Is is for the third person singular; with I we use am.
Are is for you, we and they; with I, am.
Be is the infinitive; with I you must conjugate it: am.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the table of past forms: was for I, he, she and it; were for the others. The clue is the film, third person singular (it). The right past form is was. The instruction asks for was or were, so the sentence is in the past.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The film is third person singular, which takes was.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Were is for you, we and they; the film is singular: was.
The instruction asks for the past: was.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the table of past forms: with you we always use were, even when talking to one person. The clues are yesterday afternoon, which shows the past, and the subject you. In the question the verb goes before the subject: Where were you…?
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With you the past of to be is were.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With you we always use were, also in the singular.
To be does not use the auxiliary do in questions: Where were you?
Yesterday afternoon shows the past: were.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the negative form of the present (contracted).
ejercicios.frase: She ___ at work today. She's ill.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule for the negative: add not after the verb. With she the form is is not, which contracts to isn't. The clue is the second sentence (she is ill), which explains the negative. The instruction asks for the contracted form, but is not is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With she the negative is isn't (is not).
ejercicios.traduccion: Hoy no está en el trabajo. Está enferma.

errores_previstos.explicacion: To be does not use do in the negative: isn't.
The verb is missing: she isn't (is not).
Aren't is for you, we and they; with she, isn't.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule for questions: with to be the order changes, verb before subject, and do is not used. The clue is your sister, which is the same as she and so takes is.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your sister = she: the question starts with Is, without do.

por_opcion.Is: Correct: third person singular, verb before the subject.
por_opcion.Are: Incorrect: are is for you, we and they; your sister is she.
por_opcion.Does: Incorrect: to be does not use do in questions; “Does your sister a doctor?” has no main verb.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule on the card: age is expressed with to be, not with Spanish “tener”. The clue is years old. With I, the form is am: I am 20 years old. It is one of the most typical mistakes of Spanish speakers.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: We say our age with to be.

por_opcion.have: Incorrect: calque of Spanish “tengo 20 años”; age goes with to be.
por_opcion.am: Correct: we say our age with be, and with I the form is am.
por_opcion.is: Incorrect: is is for the third person; with I, am.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule from Rules and key points: in affirmative short answers there is no contraction. The answer ends with the verb, and a contraction cannot be at the end of the sentence: Yes, I am, never “Yes, I'm”. In negative answers we do contract: No, I'm not.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In affirmative short answers there is no contraction: Yes, I am.

por_opcion.am: Correct: full form at the end of an affirmative short answer.
por_opcion.'m: Incorrect: the contraction cannot go at the end of an affirmative answer.
por_opcion.are: Incorrect: the subject of the answer is I, which takes am.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the table of past forms: with we we use were. The clues are last summer, which shows the past, and the subject we. So the verb is were, which here means Spanish “estuvimos”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Last summer shows the past and with we we use were.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estuvimos en Londres el verano pasado.

por_opcion.was: Incorrect: was is for I, he, she and it; with we, were.
por_opcion.were: Correct: past of to be with we.
por_opcion.are: Incorrect: it is present and last summer needs the past.

ejercicios.enunciado: Change the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule for questions: with to be the order changes and the verb goes before the subject, without do. They are Italian becomes Are they Italian? Note that nationality words start with a capital letter in English.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In questions with to be, the verb and the subject change places.

errores_previstos.explicacion: To be does not use do in questions: Are they Italian?
Only the intonation changes; in written English you must change the order: Are they.
With they the form is are: Are they Italian?

ejercicios.enunciado: Change the sentence into the negative.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule for the negative: add not after the verb, without do. He was happy becomes he was not happy, which contracts to wasn't. Both forms are accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: To be does not use did in the negative: he wasn't happy.
Not goes after the verb be: he was not.
With he the past is was: wasn't.

ejercicios.explicacion: This is the typical mistake on the card: in English the subject is necessary, and for the weather we use it. In Spanish “hace calor” has no subject, but in English you must say It is (It's) very hot today. The full form and the contracted form are both accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You need the subject it to talk about the weather.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the subject it is missing.
Calque of Spanish “hace calor”: in English the weather is expressed with it is.
There is means that something exists (es: “hay”) and is not used for the weather; the subject for the weather is it.

ejercicios.frase: The children was in the garden.
respuestas: The children were in the garden.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the table of past forms: were with plurals. The clue is children, the irregular plural of child, which does not end in -s but is plural. So the verb is were.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Children is plural and takes were.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños estaban en el jardín.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The children was in the garden.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: children is plural and takes were.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The childrens were in the garden.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Children is already plural; it does not take -s.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The child were in the garden.
errores_previstos.explicacion: If you change it to singular, the verb would be was; the correction needed is to change the verb: were.

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule for questions: question word + verb + subject. Where goes first, then the verb is and then the subject your office. We do not add do because the verb is be.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is the order of an indirect question (I don't know where your office is); in a direct question the verb goes before the subject.
The question word always goes first.

ejercicios.explicacion: This uses two rules from the card: being cold is expressed with to be (not with Spanish “tener”) and the negative is made with not after the verb. The order is subject + am + not + adjective. With I the contraction would be I'm not, never “I amn't”.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Not goes after the verb: I am not.
Not goes right after the verb and before the adjective: I am not cold.

descripcion_larga_es: To be is both Spanish “ser” and “estar”, and it also replaces “tener” for age, hunger, cold or fear. It is the most frequent verb in English and the base of questions, negatives and many other tenses. It is difficult for Spanish speakers because you must choose the form for each subject (am, is, are; was, were), because the subject is necessary and because age is not said with have.

contexto.que_es: It is the verb that expresses identity, origin, job, age, states, location and the weather. In the present it has three forms (am, is, are) and in the past two (was, were), with their contractions (I'm, she's, they're). It makes questions and negatives by itself, without the auxiliary do.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is the first verb you learn and it appears in almost all basic sentences: introducing yourself, describing someone, saying where you are or how you feel. It is also the auxiliary of the present continuous and the passive, so a mistake here affects all your grammar. Mistakes like “I have 30 years” or “Is very cold” show at once that the speaker is Spanish.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: Whenever you would use “ser” or “estar” in Spanish, and also instead of “tener” with age, hunger, thirst, cold, heat or fear. The signals are the subject, which decides the form, and time words (yesterday, last summer), which need the past. Spanish speakers tend to leave out the subject (it), to use do in questions and to contract in affirmative short answers.
